ASTRAEA MARINE presents the USV STOÏC 10MH, an autonomous high-seas patrol vessel designed with a patented stabilized platform that enables extended and silent maritime surveillance missions. This unique vessel uses space-connected technologies such as satellite communication and navigation (GNSS), enabling reliable real-time data transfer and precise autonomous positioning. The project addresses growing global needs for persistent maritime surveillance, border security, and environmental monitoring with minimal ecological footprint.
The USV STOÏC is equipped with a large airborne platform elevated above the water using submerged twin hulls with foils and hydrodynamic masts. This design ensures exceptional stability, making it ideal for drone deployment and recovery (both aerial and underwater). Energy autonomy is achieved through solar panels, vertical wind turbines, and biogas-powered generators, enabling several weeks of fully autonomous operations.
Our initial market targets are European maritime security agencies, environmental monitoring institutions, and defence contractors. Competitive advantages include unmatched endurance, energy autonomy via renewables, minimal acoustic and electromagnetic signature, and a modular design adaptable to a wide variety of missions.
Our revenue model includes direct sales of vessels, long-term leasing contracts, and potential technology licensing. Strategic partnerships are being pursued with drone manufacturers, maritime defence integrators, and government agencies.
In the short term, we aim to finalize industrialization, strengthen IP protection, and secure pilot clients. Over the long term, ASTRAEA MARINE intends to scale internationally, expand the USV family (different sizes, specialized missions), and become a key player in autonomous maritime solutions with strong space integration.
The core team combines deep expertise in naval engineering, renewable energy systems, and embedded technologies. Intellectual property is protected through patented design elements.

Created in 2001 to consolidate the international activities of school service centres and agencies in Quebec’s education network, Éducation internationale is a cooperative of exchange and development services in education and vocational training[1]. Éducation internationale is a non-profit cooperative comprised (and representing the majority) of Quebec’s French and English school service centres. One of the cooperative’s missions is to export Quebec’s expertise in vocational training and basic education internationally. Quebec is recognized around the world for vocational training that meets labour market needs thanks to the close ties between the labour market and vocational training centres, and the work-study opportunities available in Quebec’s vocational training system. 
 
Since its inception, Éducation internationale has led a number of international development projects in a number of African and South American countries funded by the World Bank, the African Development Bank, Global Affairs Canada, the Agence française de développement, GIZ, and the Global Partnership for Education in particular. 
 
Éducation internationale’s head office is located in Quebec City,Canada. It has legal status as a cooperative, as defined under the province of Quebec’s Cooperatives Act. Governance of the cooperative is provided by a board of directors consisting of 12directors selected by its member institutions.
[1] In Canada, provincial governments are responsible for education. As a Canadian province, Quebec has a department of education responsible for delivering educational services within its borders. In the Quebec public education system, elementary schools, secondary schools, and vocational training centres come under the authority of 72school service centres, decentralized bodies that manage and govern education and vocational training.

Environmental Performance & Sustainability:Focused on end-of-life recyclability, reduced CO₂ footprint, and minimizing debris and environmental harm during atmospheric re-entry by replacing metallic materials.

Space technology plays a crucial role: 90green integrates satellite-based Earth observation data to enhance its local measurements with broader environmental insights, such as pollutant distribution, fine dust levels, and urban heat islands. entityDescription:
I-conomy designs and manufactures state-of-the-art DC/DC converters for space applications using either qualified components or commercial components (ITAR-FREE) tested under vacuum and radiation. The team specializes in solving electro/mechanical reliability and performance issues of high voltage power supplies for space use.
I-conomy produces HV power supplies and HV custom systems guaranteed to operate in any vacuum condition so that there is no risk that outgassing of materials in space could cause dangerous discharges or corona effects.
Utilize space-use HV cables, shielded or unshielded, to distribute the high voltage to simplify assembly operations for the customer. The standard modules are contained in aluminum boxes that have 4 holes for easy and reliable fastening by screws.

For maximum vibration and shock resistance, do not use pins soldered to the PCB for control signals and power but flexible cables for effective stress release.
I-conomy also makes:
- custom high voltage systems to customer specifications to optimize weight and size, complete with mechanics, control board and HV cables
- four quadrant fast and very low noise HV modules ranging from -700V to +700V for high precision piezoelectric actuators (Fabry–Pérot interferometer applications)
